title: Enrica and Rae-Cox rhythm-and-blues catalog
summary: Welburn reads titles by the Symphonics, Butanes, Tony Rice, Shallows, Sunsets and Revelons; they charted.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: All right. So, the Enrica Records had some of the groups that was -- There was Freddie Scott and Symphonics. Their big hit was 'Come On Honey.'
Yeah.
And you had a solo on
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
that. I think we'll get a chance to listen to that. There was also the Serandettes with Teddy McRae and Orchestra -- "Boyfriend" and "The Big Night." These are 45's I'm looking at.
There's the Butanes, Teddy McRae and Orchestra. "That's My Desire" and Don't Forget I Love You.
On the Rae-Cox Label, Tony Rice and the Overtones -- "Little School Girl" and "Bluebird Of Happiness."
"Little School Girl," you say you used to release it every year --
Yeah. (Inaudible) I got to go to school.
Also on Rae-Cox, there's the Shallows?
The Shallows.
With Teddy McRae and Orchestra. "How Lucky I Am" and "Wrecking My Life."
There's the Sunsets. This is with the Eddie Wilcox Orchestra under their name. "How Will I Remember" and "Sitting and Crying."
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And then there's the Revlons -- the Revelons, rather, Teddy McRae and Orchestra. 'This Restless Heart' and 'I Promise Love' -- here's another copy of that.
Okay. So, what comments do you have about these endeavors? You --
Well most of those records were in that area -- the rock -- rhythm and blues area.
And most of --
(Inaudible) right off there, all of them hit the Billboard and Cash Box chart during their days. It was pretty good for the company.
And then later on we went into the gospel business -- gospel recording.
